summary: This program stores a player's level in a variable and prints one of two messages depending on whether that level is below 10. The `else` block guarantees the player always sees a status, even when the `if` condition is not met.

lines.text: The value stored here decides which branch runs, and 12 was chosen so the condition fails — that is how you see the `else` block do its job.
The condition in the parentheses is a question with a yes-or-no answer; the block that follows runs only when the answer is yes.
The `else` clause is the "otherwise" plan, covering every value that the condition rejected. There is no condition to write here because it handles all remaining cases.
Because 12 is not less than 10, this is the line that actually prints. Exactly one of the two blocks runs — never both, and never neither.
